# aws-api-gateway

REST vs HTTP API differences that change findings: authorizers, payload format, throttling defaults, 29s integration timeout and pricing model.

## Detected anti-patterns

### `AF-GW-001` — No `authorizationType: NONE` method on production stages (critical)

API Gateway `NONE` bypasses every authZ check at the edge; a resource method carrying it to prod is callable by the internet — the dump shows it per method, so there is no excuse to miss it.

Remediation: Require `AWS_IAM`, `CUSTOM` (Lambda authorizer) or `COGNITO_USER_POOLS` on every method exposed by production stages; keep `NONE` only for deliberately public resources, documented as such.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-GW-002` — Throttling is configured on every public stage (high)

A stage with default account-level throttling inherits limits sized for the account, not the API — one noisy neighbor or one client loop can exhaust the account's regional budget.

Remediation: Set explicit `throttlingRateLimit`/`throttlingBurstLimit` in `methodSettings` (or usage plans with API keys) sized to the backend's measured capacity, not to a guess.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-GW-003` — Access logging is enabled on every served stage (high)

Without `accessLogSettings` there is no request evidence — incident response, abuse investigation and latency attribution are all blind; enabling it later cannot recover the past.

Remediation: Set `accessLogSettings` (destination + format) per stage; include request id, integration latency, status and caller identity fields.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-GW-004` — Public stages sit behind WAF (high)

Regional API Gateway endpoints associate with AWS WAF; a public stage without a WebACL takes raw internet traffic — injection, scraping and L7 floods reach the integration unfiltered.

Remediation: Associate a WebACL with managed rule groups (+ rate rules) to public stages; log sampled requests to verify the rules fire as intended.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-GW-005` — Cache is opt-in per method with a stated TTL, never ambient (medium)

Enabling the stage cache cluster without per-method opt-in leaves capacity idle; enabling it per method without a TTL policy serves stale data silently — both are configuration smells the dump shows.

Remediation: Enable `cacheClusterEnabled` only when at least one method opts in with an explicit `cacheTtlInSeconds` and cache-key parameters named.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-GW-006` — Stages isolate environments — config drift is named (medium)

`prod` and `dev` diverging on auth, logging or throttling means the environment being tested is not the one serving users; the dump lists per-stage settings side by side precisely to surface that drift.

Remediation: Promote stage configuration through the same IaC path as deployments; diff stage settings across environments and explain every delta.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md

### `AF-GW-007` — `apiKeyRequired` is a quota tool, not authorization (medium)

API keys identify clients for usage plans and quotas; treating them as an authorization boundary fails at the first leaked key in a public client — the dump distinguishes the two attrs for a reason.

Remediation: Use `apiKeyRequired` for metering/partner identification only; real authorization comes from IAM, custom authorizers or Cognito scopes.

Reference: docs/specs/2026-09-21-api-forge-agentic-platform.md
